item.title: A Celebration of World Quality Month
item.dc:creator: Procter & Gamble
item.description:
Rapid advances in human-led, Ai-enabled predictive monitoring, real-time in-line testing, and touchless automation are taking quality management at P&G to levels of sophistication and control that would have seemed like science fiction five years ago.

— Procter & Gamble, P&G Blog (us.pg.com). Read the original

item.title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Transcript: AGM 2026
item.dc:creator: Shailesh Jejurikar, Chairman of the Board, President, and CEO
item.description:
At P&G, we are leveraging AI to help us turn insight into impact and win with consumers in all we do. We view P&G as an amplifier of human potential. Our focus is on using AI to help employees work more effectively, make better decisions, and innovate faster.

We are committed to helping P&G people build the skills needed to succeed in an AI-enabled future.

item.title: The Four Priorities Powering P&G Product Supply
item.dc:creator: Procter & Gamble
item.description:
Seamless Data and Touchless Flow is how we connect data and technology across our supply chain to make it smarter, more automated and more responsive. By connecting the right information and putting it to work through analytics, AI and automation, we can anticipate needs, make faster decisions and reduce unnecessary manual touchpoints.

P&G is also applying intelligent automation to quality control. Intelligent vision systems can perform precise quality checks, helping ensure products meet P&G’s high standards while reducing scrap waste.

— Procter & Gamble, P&G Blog (us.pg.com). Read the original

item.title: Robots Don't Build Brands. People Do.
item.dc:creator: Procter & Gamble
item.description:
The team began with a simple human observation: people protect their skin from UV exposure — why not their hair? They then combined AI with human creativity to explore consumer insights, develop concepts, land on the brand idea "Pantene Sunkiss Glow Spray for Strong Hair, Shinier than the Sun," create a package mock-up the same day and produce prototype advertising in a one-day shoot. The result: five times the assets, five times faster and at one-fifth the cost.

— Procter & Gamble, P&G Blog (us.pg.com). Read the original

item.title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Transcript: The 6th Annual Evercore Consumer & Retail Conference
item.dc:creator: Seth Cohen, CIO
item.description:
We've been focusing on harnessing that data into a core data lake, as well as the other piece that we are now able to do because of that foundational capability is our AI factory, which is where all the models sit, all of the digital products can be built upon, sit there, we can scale.

At the end of the day, I don't think there's going to be such a thing as an AI native company. I think it's just going to be a company, because everyone's going to have the AI, and the companies that have adopted it the best will be the ones that are outperforming in the marketplace.

— Seth Cohen, CIO, Investor event transcript (StockAnalysis, data by Quartr). Read the original

item.title: Seth Cohen on Accelerating AI Adoption for Lasting Business Impact
item.dc:creator: Procter & Gamble
item.description:
P&G is creating the CPG company of the future, with AI playing a key role in accelerating its transformation. At HumanX 2026, a conference that gathers 6,500 AI leaders, builders and inventors, P&G’s CIO Seth Cohen took the stage to share how the company embeds AI across its operations to turn insight into impact and deliver sustained, strong business results.

Cohen highlighted how P&G teams identified an unmet consumer need for sun protection in hair care. Using AI, they were able to rapidly develop the Pantene Sunkiss Glow Spray, moving from insight to product concept, packaging, and communications in just days instead of weeks.

Our ability to integrate data into operations is critical to enable AI. I realize AI today gets all the headlines but AI without data is simply “A” – it’s artificial.

— Procter & Gamble, P&G Blog (us.pg.com). Read the original

item.title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Transcript: Consumer Analyst Group of New York Conference (CAGNY) 2026
item.dc:creator: Seth Cohen, CIO
item.description:
Traditionally, molecular discovery has been a very costly and time-consuming process due to the needs to meet numerous technical, safety, and regulatory requirements. Typically, this process can span six to eight years of development. Our AI-powered molecular discovery suite has revolutionized this process. This groundbreaking tool, in the hands of our master scientists, allow us to identify new molecules in as little as six months.

While everyone is talking about artificial intelligence, let's be clear, AI without data is just A, artificial.

— Seth Cohen, CIO, Investor event transcript (StockAnalysis, data by Quartr). Read the original

item.title: Innovation at Scale: How P&G Transforms Business Through Technology
item.dc:creator: Procter & Gamble
item.description:
P&G's AI-driven insights have helped us better understand and anticipate your needs, reducing out-of-stock rates by 15% so products are available when and where you need them.

Technology will be integral to the future of P&G. We’re continuing to explore the latest technologies, including reasoning models and agentic AI, which may ultimately further help automate workflow and optimize supply chains and operations on an unprecedented scale.

— Procter & Gamble, P&G Blog (us.pg.com). Read the original

item.title: The Future of Collaboration: How AI is Supplementing Teamwork and Innovation at P&G
item.dc:creator: Procter & Gamble
item.description:
AI Can Be a Great “Teammate”: Research validates our approach, revealing that teams working with AI were about 12% faster. Even further, the combination of human collaboration and AI creates opportunities that enable peak performance, suggesting that the best results come from working with AI, not replacing human interaction.

“We continue to invest in training to ensure all employees become more proficient using AI technology in their respective roles to increase their impact,” said P&G Chief Information Officer Seth Cohen.

— Procter & Gamble, P&G Blog (us.pg.com). Read the original
